question: What did the US Federal Reserve decide about interest rates in September 2025, and why?
text:
On **September 17, 2025**, the Federal Reserve cut its benchmark interest rate by **0.25 percentage points**, lowering the federal funds target range from **4.25%–4.50% to 4.00%–4.25%**. ([federalreserve.gov](https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20250917a.htm?utm_source=openai))

The main reason was a **weakening labor market**: hiring had slowed, unemployment had edged up (though it remained low), and economic growth had moderated in the first half of the year. Inflation was still above the Fed’s 2% goal, but officials judged that the risk of further weakening in employment had grown enough to warrant a cut. ([federalreserve.gov](https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20250917a.htm?utm_source=openai))
